projects.name: Solar + Energy Storage on Garage
projects.description: Install 5-7 solar panels on south-facing garage roof face (20x12 ft, ~2-2.8 kW) plus battery storage. Solar = standalone ROI investment (~5yr payback at $0.42/kWh). Battery = generator alternative (no lot space for generator). 30% federal ITC applies to both when paired.
projects.notes: DESIGN: South garage face only. 5 portrait panels = 2.0 kW; 7 mixed = 2.8 kW. ~3,200-4,500 kWh/yr production (20-26% offset). All-in after ITC: solar ~$9-10k, battery ~$9-10k. VENDORS: Sunergy (sunergy.com) — EnergySage 2026 CA Installer of Year, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door. NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com) — Diamond Certified, 35yr, San Mateo County, 40yr warranty. Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy) — online only. AVOID: Sunrun.

tasks.title: Analyze energy usage and size system
tasks.notes: 17,178 kWh/yr at $0.42/kWh avg. Target: 5-7 panels south garage face (20x12 ft) = 2-2.8 kW. ~5yr payback after ITC.

tasks.title: Research and shortlist solar installers
tasks.notes: Shortlist: Sunergy (sunergy.com, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door), NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com, Diamond Certified, San Mateo County), Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy, online only). Avoid Sunrun.

tasks.title: Contact installers for quotes
tasks.notes: Spec: south garage face (20x12 ft, 5-7 panels, ~2-2.8 kW), paired battery (Enphase IQ or Powerwall 3), detached garage sub-panel interconnect. Ask each for: $/W, panel brand, inverter type, battery spec, warranty, timeline, ITC total. Request free shade/LIDAR analysis.

tasks.title: Compare quotes and select installer
tasks.notes: Prefer Enphase microinverters over string inverter. Compare $/W, battery spec, warranty, timeline. 30% ITC on full system incl. battery.

tasks.title: Confirm ITC timing — credit files in year PTO is granted
tasks.notes: 30% federal ITC on Form 5695. Claimed in tax year Permission to Operate granted by PG&E. Battery qualifies only when solar-paired. Plan install timing accordingly.

insights.summary: The sustained 18–21 connected devices alongside zero camera motion and no dog activity strongly indicates a static, quiet state—likely all occupants resting in camera-blind zones or the house being unoccupied with devices left on—rather than an active gathering or security event.

The steady increase in connected devices (15 to 19) over the last hour, paired with zero camera motion, strongly suggests unrecorded guests have arrived and are resting in camera blind spots, or a network device is stuck in a connection loop; a quick verification is recommended.

The sustained 15–20 connected devices paired with zero camera motion over four hours confirms the entire household is away from home, likely out together for a Sunday outing. This validates an empty-home state, enabling automated energy/security optimizations and alerting if pets were unexpectedly left behind.

The sustained 15–19 connected devices paired with zero camera motion on a quiet Sunday strongly indicates the household is stationary indoors (likely napping or gaming) or experiencing routine background IoT device churn, rather than an empty home or security event. This confirms the existing flag and suggests no immediate action is needed.

The combination of 15–19 connected devices with zero camera motion on a Sunday morning strongly indicates a prolonged low-activity weekend day, but the persistent lack of movement warrants verifying the cameras are active rather than offline or malfunctioning.

The sustained presence of 17–19 devices alongside zero camera motion for four hours on a weekend morning strongly indicates a camera system fault or configuration issue rather than the household being asleep. This matters because it leaves the home blind to security, pet activity, and daily routines, requiring immediate verification of camera feeds and motion detection settings.

The consistent presence of 17–19 devices combined with zero camera motion over a 4-hour weekend morning window strongly suggests the camera system is offline, motion detection is disabled, or experiencing a glitch, as it is highly unusual for two active dogs and two pre-teens to remain completely still this long.

The stable 17–19 device count paired with zero camera activity confirms both adults are awake but remaining indoors, aligning with their shared short sleep data. This coherent pattern points to early morning wakefulness rather than a departure or disruption, suggesting a gentle wellness check-in later today.

The stable 17–19 device count aligns with the expected baseline for a 4-person smart home, and combined with zero camera activity at 3:38 AM, confirms the late-night connectivity is normal background noise rather than an unusual event; the adults’ short sleep likely reflects typical family/pet-related fragmentation, suggesting a gentle morning wellness check is warranted.

The sustained presence of 17-19 active mobile devices at 2:36 AM, paired with the short sleep data for both adults, indicates a prolonged sleep disruption or late-night wakefulness rather than a brief disturbance. This suggests the household is still active, so prepare for a tired morning and consider checking on the kids or dogs.
